summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with atypical chest pain and a history of coronary artery disease, mechanical aortic valve, and recent urosepsis. Initial evaluation ruled out acute myocardial infarction with normal troponins and EKGs. Telemetry revealed frequent premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) correlating with his symptoms. A Persantine MIBI stress test showed no evidence of ischemia but confirmed fixed defects from prior infarcts and a reduced ejection fraction of 34%. EP adjusted his pacemaker settings to reduce PVC burden, and he was encouraged to adhere to metoprolol therapy. His chronic issues, including C. difficile on oral vancomycin, nephrolithiasis with hematuria, and therapeutic INR on warfarin, were managed. He improved symptomatically and was discharged home with services for follow-up with cardiology, EP, and urology, along with outpatient echo and medication reconciliation.
